businessModel: Open-source upstream funded by Google and contributors (Microsoft, Opera, Brave, Samsung and others)
updateCadence: Source tracks Chrome: new major every 2 weeks since 153; official binaries are snapshots, distro builds update via package managers
summary: The source project behind most browsers. Binaries come from distro packages or snapshots; no Google sync, no Widevine, no automatic updates, and on iOS/Android it is only an experimental or sideloaded build.
bestFor: Linux users who want a distro-packaged Blink browser
Developers and testers wanting the latest engine
Anyone building their own Chromium-based browser
notFor: Everyday users who want auto-updates and Google sync
People who need Netflix/Widevine out of the box

pros.title: Open source
pros.detail: BSD-style licensed code you can audit and build.

pros.title: No Google account tie-in
pros.detail: No Chrome sync and no Google branding, usage metrics or crash reporting.

pros.title: Distro-packaged
pros.detail: Debian, Arch, Fedora and others ship Chromium with proprietary codecs enabled by their builds.

cons.title: No auto-update
cons.detail: Official binaries lack automatic updates, so patching depends on you or your distro.

cons.title: No Widevine
cons.detail: No Netflix-style DRM by default; official builds lack licensed codecs.

cons.title: No sync
cons.detail: Chrome sync is blocked for Chromium builds since 2021.

cons.title: No MV2
cons.detail: MV2 code was removed in Chromium 151; Chrome Web Store is unofficially usable.

signatureFeatures: Basis of Chrome, Edge, Opera, Brave

faq.q: What is the difference between Chrome and Chromium?
faq.a: Chrome is Google's branded binary built on Chromium, adding auto-update, Widevine, proprietary codecs, Google sync and telemetry.

faq.q: Where do I get Chromium builds?
faq.a: Linux distributions package it; Google publishes per-commit snapshots for Windows, macOS, Linux and Android. Android builds are sideloaded APKs.
No official auto-updater. Use your package manager or fetch new snapshots.

spec.telemetry: No UMA metrics reporting in upstream builds
spec.codecs: VP8/VP9, AV1, Opus; H.264/AAC depend on build/distro ffmpeg
spec.patchSpeed: Source gets fixes immediately; binaries depend on distro or manual snapshots

privacyDefaults: No sign-in or metrics but 3P cookies
patchSpeed: Depends on distro or manual updates
telemetry: No usage stats; Google services still used
